title: Eye in Speech Bubble Emoji 👁️‍🗨️ Meaning: I Am a Witness
description: 👁️‍🗨️ was created for the “I Am A Witness” anti-bullying campaign. Today it also means “I see what you said.” Learn its origin and how people actually use it.
summary: The 👁️‍🗨️ eye in speech bubble emoji means “I am a witness.” It was created for an anti-bullying campaign so people could show support when they saw someone being harassed online. Many now use it more loosely for watching, noticing or “I see what's going on here.”
meaning: Unlike nearly every other emoji, this one was made for a cause. It is the symbol of “I Am A Witness,” a campaign launched by the Ad Council in 2015 to encourage teenagers who see bullying to speak up. The idea was simple: when someone is being attacked in a comment thread, bystanders post 👁️‍🗨️ to tell the target they are not alone and to tell the bully that people are watching.

The design states the message directly. An eye, for witnessing, sits inside a speech bubble, for saying something. Technically it is a combination of two existing emojis, 👁️ and 🗨️, joined by an invisible connector, which is how it could be added to phones without a brand-new character being encoded. Apple shipped it soon after the campaign began, and other vendors followed.

The campaign meaning never became common knowledge. Most people who stumble on the emoji have no idea why it exists, and that has produced a second, improvised life. It gets used for “seen,” for lurking in a group chat, for keeping an eye on someone, or as an eerie, surreal decoration. Read-receipt jokes are a frequent home: the eye in the bubble looks like a message that has been viewed.

It also turns up in posts about accountability and observation more broadly, such as whistleblowing, journalism, surveillance and “I saw what you posted before you deleted it.” Because it is unfamiliar, it can come across as cryptic or slightly menacing when sent without explanation. Anyone using it for its original purpose is wise to add a few words of support alongside.

contexts.label: Against bullying
contexts.body: The intended use is as a reply when someone is being mocked or harassed. Posting 👁️‍🗨️ signals that you have noticed and that you stand with the person targeted. Schools and youth organizations still reference it in anti-bullying lessons. Since few bullies or victims recognize it, a short supportive sentence makes the gesture far more effective.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Friends use it playfully for “I saw that.” It answers a suspicious story post, a deleted message or a group chat confession. It can also mean “I'm watching this unfold” when drama is brewing. The tone is usually teasing, a quirkier alternative to 👀.

contexts.label: On social media
contexts.body: It appears in bios and captions for an offbeat, mysterious look, and in replies that call out hypocrisy or receipts. Accounts focused on media criticism, privacy and surveillance use it thematically. On posts where someone is being piled on, a few users still deploy it in the campaign sense.

contexts.label: On unsupported devices
contexts.body: Where the sequence is not recognized, it breaks into its ingredients and displays as an eye next to a speech bubble. Recipients then see two unrelated symbols and may be confused. This is rarer than it once was, but it is a reason the emoji never spread as widely as its creators hoped.

examples.text: That comment was out of line. 👁️‍🗨️ We see you, and we've got your back, Maya.
examples.meaning: Publicly supporting someone being bullied, in the emoji's original sense.
A teasing “I noticed what you did.”

examples.text: Reading the group chat and saying nothing 👁️‍🗨️
examples.meaning: Admitting to lurking and watching the conversation.
A warning that what was posted has been seen and recorded.
A joke about being left on read.

examples.text: If you see bullying, say something 👁️‍🗨️
examples.meaning: An awareness message urging bystanders to act.

combos.meaning: Witnessing and standing in solidarity with someone.
Seen and screenshotted; there is evidence.
Watching closely and making it known.
A stand against bullying or harassment.

confusedWith.difference: 👀 is the everyday emoji for looking, noticing gossip or showing interest. It is casual and universally understood. 👁️‍🗨️ adds the idea of speaking up about what was seen, and many recipients will not know it at all.
👁️ is a single eye, used for watching, the “I see” pun or mystical imagery. It is one of the two components of this emoji. The speech bubble around it is what turns observation into testimony.

🗨️ is the other component, an empty bubble that only means speech or comment. On devices that cannot combine the sequence, the two parts appear separately, which is where the confusion usually starts.

avoid: Do not send it without context to someone who might find an unexplained eye unsettling.
Avoid assuming it will be understood as anti-bullying support; say so in words as well.
Do not use it to intimidate, as in implying that you are monitoring a person.
design: An eye centered inside a speech bubble. On Apple and several other platforms the bubble is dark with a light outline of an eye, giving it the look of a logo more than a drawing; other vendors show a more literal eye in a white bubble. It is a sequence of 👁️ and 🗨️, so appearance varies more between platforms than for most emojis.

faqs.a: Officially, “I am a witness.” It was designed for an anti-bullying campaign so bystanders could signal support for someone being harassed. In casual use it has broadened to “I see this” or “I'm watching.”

faqs.q: Why was the eye in speech bubble emoji created?
faqs.a: The Ad Council introduced it in 2015 for its “I Am A Witness” campaign, which asked teens to stop being silent bystanders to bullying. Technology companies supported the effort by adding the symbol to their emoji keyboards.

It can look that way if the recipient does not know its background, since a lone eye suggests surveillance. Its purpose is the opposite: protective and supportive. A brief explanation removes most of the strangeness.

faqs.q: Why do I see an eye and a speech bubble separately?
faqs.a: Your device or app does not support the combined sequence, so it shows the two emojis it is made from. The sender chose a single emoji. Updating software generally fixes the display.

faqs.q: Does 👁️‍🗨️ mean a message was seen?
faqs.a: Not officially. No major app uses it as a read receipt. People borrow it for jokes about being left on read because an eye in a chat bubble neatly suggests a viewed message.
